result: Exact release source shows both UpdateTaskParams and CancelTaskParams have a serde field renamed _meta with type Option<RequestMetaObject>, and both constructors initialize meta to None. Therefore a caller that explicitly sets params.meta before using the existing update_task/cancel_task helper has a source-defined serialization path for params._meta; the helpers' Request::new(params) construction does not by itself erase that field. This narrows the remaining uncertainty to RequestMetaObject's own arbitrary-key serde representation and server-side RequestParamsMeta exposure, not the two task param structs themselves.
evidence_scope: Exact rmcp-v3.1.4 model.rs only. The run also observed Request<M,P>::new creates default request extensions, but this finding is limited to task params._meta serialization presence. No claim is made that arbitrary custom keys inside RequestMetaObject round-trip byte-for-byte, that every transport preserves them, that server RequestContext exposes them unchanged, or that any generation token is atomically enforced.
